storage: local Docker named volume; loopback HTTP; no TLS or artificial network delay
limitations: Short probes identify candidate rates, not sustained or 30-day capacity.
Shared host workloads may affect results; no other containers are stopped.
SDK events and adapter wire output are recorded once, then replayed with new identities.
Verification retains encoded replay descriptions, releases them page by page and accumulates per-view summaries; every complete payload is reconstructed and checked after restart.
OTLP batching and gzip model a gateway; SDK adapters still send one event per request.
Request latency starts after serialization/compression; preparation and schedule lag are reported separately.
Resource sampling includes Docker exec overhead and may miss peaks. Container memory includes filesystem cache.
Scheduled retention scans run every five seconds with a 30-day TTL; these runs do not measure deletion of expired data.

Optional aggregate profiling covers the process lifetime, including preload, health checks and startup retention, but excludes schema initialization and final checkpoint. It is unavailable after SIGKILL. Queue depth and internal timing percentiles are not measured.
Image ID identifies the executable. Git source provenance is the local checkout and cannot attest to a separately supplied image.

measurement_notes: The wrapper stopped and restored 13 development containers. The generic runner limitation saying no other containers are stopped does not apply to this run.

The immutable image ID, collector source hashes, workload plan and service thresholds match stability-retry-2026-10-19.json. Container RAM changed from 2048 to 4096 MiB and its proportional safety guard from 1800 to 3600 MiB. DuckDB automatic memory_limit changed from 1.5 to 3.1 GiB. CPU stayed at 2, with no container swap.
The collector source is pinned to the earlier capacity implementation. Browser/OS/device query filters added after that source revision are not exercised by this image.

The full 300-second offer completed, but both performance pass flags are false. There were 48411 HTTP 503 responses and all three aggregate query p95 values exceeded 500 ms. The generator omitted 699 scheduled requests for lateness. The observed successful request rate is not an established sustainable capacity.

The durable queue approached its default 67108864-byte pending payload budget. Its peak sampled pending_bytes was 67108774. HTTP failure bodies are not retained, so queue exhaustion is supported by this correlation, not a per-rejection reason counter.

The first queue sample after HTTP completion had 35118 pending events. The queue was observed empty after a completed 12787.14 ms wait, before graceful shutdown. The oldest queued event after HTTP completion was 19453 ms old. The HTTP 202 latency measures spool acknowledgement, not DuckDB visibility.

All sampled cgroup memory.high, memory.max, OOM and OOM-kill event counters, and memory PSI some/full totals, were zero through traffic and queue drain. This does not describe host memory pressure. The Mac host had swap and compression activity during the broader sample interval.
Host memory samples cover preload, traffic, verification and restoration. Cumulative vm_stat deltas cannot attribute memory activity to one process or phase.

Aggregate profiles include preload, traffic, queue drain, health checks and retention. Writer requests/transactions count replay batches, not individual HTTP requests. prepare_request is outside the measured ingest execution interval.

The runner gracefully restarted and verified all 900890 acknowledged events, including 50000 preload events. Payload, browser/IP context, original OTLP envelope, pagination, global summary and per-video summary checks passed. No persisted event lacked an acknowledgement. The disposable container and volume were removed.
